lesson.menu_title: Handling Pushback -- Responding to Objections Calmly
lesson.menu_desc: Answer a skeptical partner from Verona: acknowledge the concern, reframe the idea, and keep your position politely, with 'I can see why you might think that, but...' -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 27 -- Handling Pushback
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Flávia Florêncio Ferreira | Lesson 27 -- Handling Pushback
lesson.grammar_point: handling objections (acknowledge, reframe and hold your position: I can see why you might think that, but / let me put it a different way / with respect, I would maintain that)

listenings.text: Hello, Flavia. This is Lorenzo Conti, from the trade association in Verona. Thank you for the documents. Before our meeting on Monday, I want to share three concerns from our members. First, the price. Brazilian products are far away, so the transport is expensive. Second, quality. Our buyers want proof that every product meets European standards. Third, the timeline. They want to see results in less than one year. I am not saying no. I am saying that we need clear answers. See you on Monday.

Objections are not a bad sign. When a partner pushes back, it often means that they are interested. Here is a simple method. First, acknowledge the concern. Say: I understand your concern. Do not argue right away. Second, clarify. Ask a question to understand the real problem. Third, reframe. Show the idea from a different point of view. Finally, if you believe in your position, keep it, politely. And if you need time, it is fine to pause. A short silence is better than a weak answer.

extra_audio.text: First, I listen to the objection and I do not interrupt. Then, I acknowledge the concern: I understand your concern. Next, I ask a question to clarify the real problem. After that, I reframe the idea: let me put it a different way. Finally, I keep my position politely and I propose a next step.

items.situation: A partner says: "Your process is too slow." Acknowledge the concern first.
tips: and I think it is worth clarifying the timeline.

items.situation: The partner did not understand your idea. Say it in a new way.
tips: Let me put it a different way:
what we are building is a framework that protects producers.

items.situation: The partner says the pilot is a bad idea. Keep your position, politely.
tips: With respect, I would maintain that

items.situation: The partner asks a very difficult question. Buy some time.
tips: Give me a moment to consider that.

items.situation: The partner has doubts about quality. Acknowledge and add a fact.
tips: That is a fair point. What I would add is that
our certified producers have an audit every year.
